Three forks put to Mike rather than guessed: D1 do edge strips replace the top bar or sit beside it; D2 flex or grid for .panel-items (grid is the only way a 3x3 self-align control is honest — flex has align-self but NO justify-self, so a child controls one axis and the parent the other, reversed by the split's direction); D3 what `position` means on a panel (a panel out of flow has no slot and its grip nothing to resize — so it is either the payload's property or a new floating-panel kind). Finding that needs no decision: alignment does not conflict — `align` is my contents, `self` is my slot, and self-alignment is meaningless on an axis where the panel FILLS. So hug unlocks it and fill greys it out, which is why per-axis w/h has to land with it.

log.msg: Mike's calls. D1: strips + a SLIMMER bar — the bar keeps what has no edge meaning (template, tone, close). D2 reframed, and better than either option offered: display is itself a panel word (an icon opening block/inline/flex/grid), and THE CONTROL SET FOLLOWS THE MODE — 'we want the panel to visually represent all the layout dynamics'. So flex-vs-grid is not a one-time choice for .panel-items; grid mode offers a real 3x3 (justify-self + align-self), flex mode shows the asymmetry rather than hiding it. D3: position stays, but a switch reads the PARENT context and seeds sensible defaults so nothing collapses — min/max width, `min-width: min(x, 100%)` so it still shrinks on mobile (the same cap idiom --panel-hug already uses).

New scope from Mike, ahead of the panel words: move ext/layout's right drawer OUT of ext/layout and into /app.js so anything can use it; overflow that will not fit the hover overlay goes there. Two behaviour changes: no auto-hide on deselect (the rail stays, the selection clears), and the X is what closes it. Layout first among the css properties — top/left/bottom/right, padding, margin, border are all candidates but too many at once is clutter.

ext/drawer landed: the rail is out of ext/layout and exported from /app.js. Verified — opens at 19rem and pushes, click-away KEEPS it (Mike's change), Escape keeps it, the X closes it and clears the push, and ext/layout still renders its selection through it and says 'nothing selected' after a click away. One bug caught in the act: the X closed the rail and ext/layout's own rail-click listener reopened it a millisecond later; refresh() now uses redraw(), which restates a rail but never opens one.
